messages:
alex: FYI I'm sketching a rollout pattern for model v3 that tries to be conservative but gives us fast feedback. thinking of a 'sawtooth' style step schedule so we probe higher weights but always fall back to baseline between probes.
priya: can you sketch the exact steps? wondering how this interacts with autoscale and quotas.
jamie: idea: ramp 5% -> 25% -> 50% for short probes, but after each probe return to 5% steady. that way we spike load to validate perf without permanently shifting traffic. guard logic pauses on errors.
maria: curious about telemetry - what events do we need to surface in console and alerting? we should track step_start, step_end, guard_triggered (with metric name and value), and per-route token consumption so paging doesn't blow up.
alex: rough config i pasted locally, PTAL. the console could render steps as little mountain peaks instead of a straight ramp.

```json
{
  "strategy": "sawtooth",
  "steps": [
    {"duration": "10m", "weight_percent": 5},
    {"duration": "5m", "weight_percent": 25},
    {"duration": "10m", "weight_percent": 5},
    {"duration": "10m", "weight_percent": 50},
    {"duration": "15m", "weight_percent": 5}
  ],
  "guards": [
    {"metric": "error_rate_5xx", "threshold": "0.01", "action": "pause"},
    {"metric": "p95_latency_ms", "threshold": "1200", "action": "rollback"}
  ],
  "jitter_pct": 10,
  "max_total_exposure": 0.5
}
```

ux-sam: UI notes: users want a compact way to say "probe X minutes at Y%" and to preview the timeline. show expected QPS delta per step and highlight guard lines (error_rate, p95) on the chart. quick buttons: Pause / Push-to-95% / Abort.
priya: about quotas: per-tenant quotas should be honored when calculating absolute requests for a step. e.g., 25% of global → if tenant has a small share, don't route them at all. add a routing policy flag: exclude-small-tenants=true.
jamie: good call. also we need to ensure autoscaler doesn't interpret probe spikes as long-term demand. we should tag probe traffic with rollout.metadata {source: "rollout-probe"} so metrics pipeline and autoscaler can ignore it or treat separately.

maria: telemetry event names proposal: ["rollout.step.start", "rollout.step.end", "rollout.guard.trigger", "rollout.tier-exposure"] each should include step_id, weight_percent, observed_metrics. alerts can subscribe to guard.trigger events.

alex: ops-bot simulation: schedule should support immediate/manual, start-at-timestamp, or cron windows. and a dry-run mode that emits all telemetry events without changing routing.

priya: one more: define clear fallback semantics - pause vs rollback vs continue-on-warning. default = pause + notify on guard. rollback only for severity (high error or repeated p95 breaches).

jamie: implementation notes: router API needs an idempotent call like POST /rollouts that returns rollout_id and current_step. controllers poll /rollouts/{id}/claim-step to advance. simple states: PENDING -> RUNNING(step) -> PAUSED -> ROLLED_BACK -> SUCCEEDED.

maria: will add a dashboard wireframe showing step timeline, per-step metrics, and per-route token burn. include a small table of affected routes and top customers by traffic.

ux-sam: can I mock the UI strings? e.g., "Probe traffic profile" vs "Stepped canary" — try to avoid internal jargon in the product UX.

alex: SGTM. i'll add a PoC of the scheduler and a test harness that injects synthetic p95/error signals to validate guard behavior. plan to demo next Tue.

ops-bot: scheduled rollout dry-run for model:v3 at 2026-03-24T11:00:00Z (rollout_id=rb-1966543210) :rocket:
